# Building the American dream: How JPMorganChase is helping a North Texas manufacturer grow


From left: Stevie Baron, CEO of Business Banking at Chase; Nick Such, Lexington, KY; Amy Oraefo, Atlanta, GA; Carlos Pereira, Las Vegas, NV; Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorganChase; Kimberly Ransom, Indianapolis, IN; Tony Woodall, Grand Prairie, TX. Credit: JPMorganChase

For Tony Woodall, the American Dream has always been simple: own a business, create opportunities for others and build something he’s proud of.


After spending 18 years working for a large corporation, Woodall was ready to take a leap.


In 2006, he had the opportunity to acquire a small waterjet cutting company in Grand Prairie. He saw more than a niche business. He saw the foundation for something much bigger.


The challenge was finding the capital to make it happen.


Working with his local Chase banker, Woodall secured financing that helped him purchase the company and begin investing in its future.


“I’ve always believed the American Dream is owning your own business,” said Woodall, owner of AST Manufacturing. “In 2006, I was able to make that dream a reality and become a business owner, and that wouldn’t be possible without financing from Chase.”


Nearly two decades later, the small waterjet business has evolved into AST Manufacturing, a full-service metal fabrication and advanced manufacturing company serving industries where precision and reliability are critical, including aerospace, defense, medical equipment, automotive and energy.


Woodall’s journey reflects the work behind JPMorganChase’s American Dream Initiative – a multi-year effort aimed, in part, at helping more small business owners access the capital, guidance, tools, and connections they need to start, grow, and scale.


Through the initiative, JPMorganChase aims to[power 10 million small businesses](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/american-dream-initiative-announcement) over the next several years, combining direct support for owners with practical policy solutions designed to remove barriers to opportunity and growth.


Today, Woodall’s focus is on keeping pace with demand.


“Our biggest challenges as a small business are two-fold: we are having a difficult time hiring employees who specialize in our area of work and we’re blessed with more business than we can possibly complete, so we need more machinery and a bigger space,” Woodall said.


Those challenges recently brought Woodall to Washington, D.C., where he joined four other small business owners from around the country to meet directly with policymakers and discuss what it takes to grow a business in today’s economy.


The conversations gave business owners an opportunity to share firsthand experiences and highlight the obstacles they face as they work to expand, hire and compete.


One thing stood out to Woodall. Although each owner represented a different business and industry, many were facing the same challenges.


Access to capital remains essential for businesses looking to invest in equipment, technology and facilities. Finding skilled workers continues to be a challenge across many industries. And for smaller businesses, competing for larger procurement opportunities can be difficult without the right resources and professional networks.


“Tony’s experience reflects what we hear from small business owners across the country: access to capital is essential, but sustainable growth also requires skilled workers, a disciplined management team, strong business connections and opportunities to compete,” said Marcus Kline, Southwest Texas Market Manager at Chase for Business and member of the Central Texas Market Leadership Team. “Through the American Dream Initiative, we’re focused on bringing those pieces together so more entrepreneurs can scale sustainably.”


JPMorganChase is focused on providing practical ways to strengthen the small business ecosystem through the American Dream Initiative, and help more owners like Woodall turn ambition into growth.


For instance, the company plans to provide approximately $80 billion in small business lending over the next decade, while[supporting practical policy solutions](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/content/dam/jpmorganchase/documents/newsroom/adi-powering10m-smb-report.pdf) it believes can help ensure small business owners can access the right financing at the right time.


For Woodall, the next chapter is focused on meeting demand and continuing to invest in the future of AST Manufacturing. As the company expands its capacity, hires new talent, and serves more customers across Texas, he remains focused on the same goal that inspired him to take a leap nearly two decades ago: building something that lasts.
